mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with FEDFUNDS change (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by monthly PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 new jobs, signaling labor market strength that supports equity risk appetite and drives positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Payroll growth does not exceed 200,000 for 3 consecutive months, or 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (GDPC1) by more than 5% in a month indicates weakening aggregate demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by >5% in a single month
failure_condition: GDPC1 declines by <=5% in all subsequent months, or 5-day forward returns remain non-negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the INDX of manufacturing production (INDPRO) below 100 for two consecutive months suggests supply-side softness that raises equity risk premia, producing negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 100 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: INDPRO remains above 100 for 3 months, or 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 0.4% for three consecutive months, the market anticipates a policy shift and sells equities in advance, generating negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises above 0.4% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL remains below 0.4% for 4 months, or 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising unemployment rates (UNRATE) above 4% indicate weakening labor demand, which is associated with negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as risk aversion increases.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4% and remains above for 2 months
failure_condition: UNRATE stays below 4% for 3 months, or 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both HOUST (housing starts) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 10% in the same month creates a dual-demand shock that predicts negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by >=10% AND RSAFS falls by >=10% in the same month
failure_condition: Neither HOUST nor RSAFS falls by >=10% in any month, or 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains above 5% for four consecutive months in a low-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL < 2.5%), the market expects persistent tightening, which drives positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as rates are expected to stabilize.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% for 4 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < 2.5%
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS does not stay above 5% for 4 months, or CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5% during the period, or 60-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05).
